title: Interlock Window Orchestration with Regional Fallbacks and Communication Playbook
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Objective: Create a single playbook and execution plan that coordinates cutover windows across runtime, Console, and API teams with explicit regional fallback lanes, communication templates, and automated gating. Scope: multi-surface launches affecting hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Console dashboards; includes Canary cohorts, capacity reservations, and a two-tier fallback plan (model-variant downgrade and regional failover). Success metrics: zero P0 Sev during cutover windows across regions; <2% user API error rate spike; rollback/mitigate within 20 minutes of escalation trigger. This ticket coordinates owners, defines preflight gates, post-cutover verification checklists, and runbook templates for on-call and product leads.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook docs reviewed and approved by Runtime, Console, API, and SRE
Canary cohorts and traffic shaping policies codified in routing config repo
Communication templates (customer, internal ops, support) created and staged
Escalation matrix validated in tabletop exercise with true/false simulation
Automated smoke checks and rollback conditions implemented in release orchestration
deliverables: Interlock window playbook (Confluence) - includes blackout matrices and capacity gates
Preflight checklist (Google Sheet) with owner signoffs
Regional fallback runbooks for eu-west-1 / us-west-2 / ap-southeast-1
Communication templates: incident, cutover notice, rollback notice
Automation PRs for canary routing and smoke tests (github.com/redwood/release-orchestration)
risks: Underestimated cross-region capacity contention during simultaneous launches
Delayed approvals from compliance for Private deployment changes
Ambiguous ownership of failover steps between Runtime and API teams
Insufficient test coverage for model-variant downgrade compatibility
